Your router does not share which ports are open.
Decoy file server
A fake storage box on your network that sends you an alert when someone opens it.
Shows up on your network as %1$s
It shows up next to your real devices, with shared folders and a login page. Signing in or opening a folder sends you an alert.
Intrusion detection
Checks what reaches your DeKoi against known attack patterns.
The patterns come from a list that security researchers keep up to date. They arrive with your DeKoi’s weekly update.
Scan detection
Notices a device searching your network for devices or openings.
Before an intruder tries anything, they look around. Your DeKoi notices a device trying address after address, or opening after opening.
ARP Guard
Notices a device pretending to be another, such as your router.
A device that pretends to be your router can read what others send. Your DeKoi notices when a second device claims an address that is taken.
Router Guard
Notices a second device handing out network settings or announcing itself as your router.
Only your router should tell devices how to reach the internet. Another device doing it can send their traffic its own way.
Name trap
Asks for names that do not exist, to catch a device that answers anyway.
Every few minutes your DeKoi asks your network for names nobody uses. Normal devices stay quiet. A device that answers is trying to catch sign-ins.
Notices a copy of your Wi-Fi nearby.
Your DeKoi checks the Wi-Fi networks around it with its own radio. A network with your name and weaker protection is a copy, set up to lure your devices.
Network map
Shows the devices on your network and what each one looks like.
Your DeKoi listens to what devices say about themselves, and recognises phones, TVs, printers and more.
New device alerts
Tells you when a device joins your network for the first time.
Your first day with DeKoi counts as your household. After that, every device it has not seen before gets an alert.
Internet check
Checks your internet every minute, and that web addresses lead where they should.
Every minute your DeKoi checks your router and the internet. Every hour it compares web address lookups with an independent service, to notice a router that sends you to the wrong place.
Lists what your router has opened to the internet, and tells you about new openings.
Devices can ask your router to let the internet in. Your DeKoi reads that list every hour and never changes it.
A short note once a week: alerts, new devices and time online.
Once a week you get a short note with three numbers: alerts, new devices, and how much of the week your DeKoi was online.
